 by Kris Kuyper
 Sun, October 25, 2026 at 4:00 AM This big upper low well off of California should eventually bring us a little rain next weekend. Comment on this story 1 Comment Share story Share topics: 
 Halloween 
 Rain 
 Weather 
 San Joaquin Valley 
 Forecast 
 Black cat 
 Wet weather 
 Friday 
 Our weather was nice on Saturday in the San Joaquin Valley, and Sunday's might be even a little better - and that should continue through the middle of the week. But that's where a black cat runs across this forecast, and changes our luck: wet weather returns by Friday, and could linger through next weekend - which includes Halloween!
 Our weekend started with fog in a few places in the Valley, and our first Dense Fog Advisory of the season! We had a LOT of those last year, but we shouldn't see as many this year - our upcoming El Nino winter weather pattern should keep us too unsettled for weeks of quiet, foggy weather like we had last January & February. After the patchy (but dense) fog burned off Saturday morning, Merced warmed up to 71 in the afternoon, Madera and Hanford reached 72, while Fresno topped out at 73.
 Sunday... and Monday... & Tuesday and Wednesday... should all see mostly sunny skies, with little to no fog, and highs in the middle to upper 70's. Not a bad finish to October at all.
 Above: Tracking the strengthening El Niño in the Pacific, and talking about how 2 similarly strong El Niño's can bring very different results to California's rainy season.
 That all changes by Thursday, as a storm from the central Pacific will approach California. We should remain dry, but clouds will move in.
 It's Friday that should see a return of the wet weather, although it doesn't look like a whole lot - just light showers that might give us 1/10" of rain. Probably a little less, so it won't be a washout.
 That looks like it will continue through the weekend, which includes Halloween on Saturday night. I know, not the best timing from Mother Nature.
 BUT... it's not a big storm at all, and there definitely will be big breaks in the rain. It's too early to time those breaks out, but I'll be doing that later in the week. I remember how much fun I had as a little trick-or-treater, and my kids loved it as well, so we've got to get the little ones out there and knock on some doors Saturday night - I'm sure there will be at least some windows of dry weather to find!
 One more thing about Halloween night - don't forget to Fall Back! Set your clocks back 1 hour - we'll get an extra hour of sleep Sunday morning, because that's when Daylight Saving Time ends. 
 But no sleeping in this morning - Sunday looks to good to waste. With lots of sun, and highs in the upper 70's, it'll be great weather to pick a pumpkin from the patch!
